subject: Runtime locations, subprocessor chain, and export-control checklist
messages:
From: Elena Marcus <elena.marcus@aureliahealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, security@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Runtime locations and subprocessors — initial questions

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security and legal teams so we can evaluate the integration risk and present a concise summary to our procurement committee:

1) Where do inference requests execute (regionally)? Do you guarantee processing inside the EU when we pick an EU tenancy, or are there transient hops to non-EU infra/subprocessors?
2) Which subprocessors touch request text or derived artifacts (e.g., cache, metrics)? Please call out their primary location (country/region) and role.
3) For cross-border transfers, do you rely on SCCs, adequacy, or customer-specific contractual guards? Any planned third-country exports we should expect?
4) Deletion: after we mark an account for shutdown, what is your timeline for active data purge and for backups/replicas? Do you offer an on-demand purge for enterprise customers?

Can you reply with a short, exportable section we can paste into an internal memo? Attachments (inventory or diagrams) would be helpful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Marcus
Director, Information Security
Aurelia Health

Subject: Re: Runtime locations and subprocessors — initial questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can drop into your memo; attaching a topology diagram and our current subprocessor inventory as CSV. Happy to hop on a short call if you want more granularity.

Summary (short):
- Regional execution: Customers select a deployment region (EU: eu-west-1 or eu-central-1). When an EU tenancy is selected, inference execution, temporary KV cache, and storage of ephemeral artifacts remain in EU regions by default.
- Transient hops: Control-plane metadata (non-PII) is routed via our control plane which operates in multiple regions; we do not store customer request payloads in the control plane. Network paths may transit other regions for routing, but all persisted request or inference artifacts remain in the selected region unless the customer authorizes cross-region processing.
- Subprocessors touching requests: FastCloud Compute (compute hosts) — primary EU fleet; StorageHub (object store) — EU buckets; KeySafe KMS (key management) — customer-key option (EU-backed HSM available); MetricsRelay (aggregated telemetry) — anonymized metrics, sampled and persisted outside request payloads. Full inventory attached.
- Cross-border guards: We rely on a combination of adequacy decisions for EU-resident customers where applicable and EU SCCs embedded in our DPA. Any export outside the EU is gated by customer configuration and documented in the DPA; by default we do not export inference data for EU tenancies.
- Deletion timelines: Active customer data (indexes, stored contexts, KV cache) is deleted within 30 days after account termination by default. Snapshots/backups are scheduled for deletion within 90 days; customers with enterprise commitments can request an expedited on-demand purge (we support 5–15 day accelerations depending on scope).

Attachments: redwood_processing_topology_v1.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_2026-11.csv

Quick asks if you want more: (a) confirm if you need SCCs + DPA countersigned, (b) whether you want a dedicated EU-only key material (we can enable a customer-managed key in EU), (c) expected retention SLA if you require <30d active retention.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks — if easier we can take these on a 30-minute call.

Subject: Re: Runtime locations and subprocessors — initial questions

Samir / Elena — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Telemetry/PII in traces:
- We instrument tracing and metrics to surface latency and error signals. Traces and telemetry do not contain request payloads or user PII by design. Any identifiers are hashed and sampled; we redact header-level tokens before they reach MetricsRelay. If you need, we can add an additional filter layer that strips custom headers before telemetry emission.

2) SCCs and DPA:
- We include the EU SCCs in our standard DPA for customers that select EU residency. We can provide a countersigned template and keep the negotiation minimal for procurement. I'll include a DPA draft link in the deal record.

3) KV cache TTL and configurability:
- Default prefix KV TTL: 24 hours for ephemeral inference caches. You can configure the TTL per-route; we can set TTL=0 (disable caching) for your tenancy or for specific routes if you prefer zero persistence. Note: disabling caching increases per-token cost and may affect latency on repeated prefixes.

4) Subprocessor legal mapping (CSV):
- Attached inventory maps the operating name to legal entity and country. Quick callouts: FastCloud Compute AS (EU) — compute; StorageHub Europe Ltd (Ireland) — object storage; KeySafe Global AB (EU HSM offering) — KMS (customer-key option available).

Next steps:
- I'll attach an export-friendly paragraph you can paste into procurement and drop a DPA + SCCs link into the HubSpot deal.
- If you want an accelerated purge option on termination, we can add a term to the SOW (expedited purge within 10 business days).

Pasteable paragraph for procurement:
"Redwood will execute inference and persist only ephemeral artifacts within the customer-selected EU region (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1). Persisted data is deleted within 30 days after termination, with backups deleted within 90 days; an enterprise expedited purge (10 business days) is available by contract. Subprocessors that touch request data are listed in the attached inventory and are contractually bound by our DPA which embeds EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Telemetry is sampled and redacted of PII prior to export to analytics subprocessors."

I'll upload the DPA/SCCs template to the HubSpot deal and share the link momentarily. Looping Marissa to confirm we have the right legal names in the CSV. Jonas — can you confirm the EU-HSM option is available for AH and whether there are any additional setup steps?

Best,
Connor
